user-code-on-own-domain-01.graded_text: The target layout serves people's HTML and JavaScript from a separate registrable domain, not from any subdomain of plinth.example.

votes.e: B/project/docs/hosting-plan.md: "Run user HTML and JavaScript in a frame on a **separate registrable content domain**, with one stable origin per app." It also rejects the subdomain alternative: "Moving content under another path or another `*.plinth.example` host ... does not solve this problem."

user-code-on-own-domain-02.graded_text: The reason given is that every subdomain of one registrable domain is the same site: script on a sibling subdomain can set cookies for the parent domain and ride same-site requests, which lets it interfere with sign-in (login CSRF or session confusion) or reach session tokens.

votes.e: B/project/docs/hosting-plan.md: "Different HTTPS subdomains have different origins, but share a site when they have the same registrable domain... A cookie scoped to `plinth.example` is sent to its subdomains, and a sibling document can set parent-domain cookies... user code can read script-accessible session material or attempt cookie shadowing and session fixation." It adds: "`SameSite` is not a sibling-subdomain isolation boundary."

user-code-on-own-domain-03.graded_text: The short <name>.plinth.example address is kept as Plinth's own page, which frames the app served from the other domain, so visitors still see the Plinth address.

votes.e: B/project/docs/hosting-plan.md target table: "`https://<name>.plinth.example`; trusted viewer, private-access gate, metadata and framing". It also says: "Keep the visible short URL rather than redirecting visitors to the runtime."

user-code-on-own-domain-04.graded_text: Each app gets its own origin on the content domain, such as a label per app, so one app cannot read another's storage.

votes.e: B/project/docs/hosting-plan.md: "App runtime | `https://<appId>.CONTENT_DOMAIN`" and "Use an immutable, non-sensitive app ID for the runtime hostname... a different app never inherits an old app ID."

user-code-on-own-domain-05.graded_text: Until the separate domain can be set up after the freeze, people's code runs with an opaque origin, through a sandbox (for example a CSP sandbox header) without allow-same-origin, and the plan says this costs the apps their browser storage. It does not keep serving people's code as the top-level document on plinth.example subdomains during the beta.

votes.e: B/project/docs/hosting-plan.md does say the sandbox costs storage ("`Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts` ... Omit `allow-same-origin` ... It blocks `document.cookie` and `localStorage`"), and it does stop top-level serving on plinth.example. But that sandbox is only an optional internal preview ("If an internal containment preview is needed..."), not how people's code runs during the beta. The beta decision is "**no-go for the advertised beta next week while the freeze remains unchanged**. Keep publication closed and serve trusted holding pages at short addresses". The sandboxed beta is handed to the owner as an open option: "the owner must choose a freeze exception or explicitly accept the reduced, storage-free sandbox scope... This plan assumes neither choice". So the plan never commits to running people's code under an opaque origin during the freeze.

blocking: [claude] B/project/docs/hosting-plan.md does not ship a beta layout for people's apps. It says "My recommendation is therefore **no-go for the advertised beta next week**" and "serve trusted holding pages at short addresses", then leaves the actual call to the owner: "If opening next week is mandatory, the owner must choose a freeze exception or explicitly accept the reduced, storage-free sandbox scope... This plan assumes neither choice". The prompt asked for 'the hosting and origin layout we should ship' and to 'make the calls you can'. An opaque-origin sandbox on the existing hosts was a safe beta layout that needed no new infrastructure, and the plan itself describes it, but it does not pick it. An engineer reading this tomorrow can only build holding pages.
